message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of practical steps you can take to keep your piano sounding its best and extending its life: | Maintenance Area | What to Do | Why It Matters | |-------------------|------------|---------------| | **Humidity & Temperature** | • Keep indoor air between 45‑55 % RH (relative humidity).
• Use a hygrometer near the piano.
• Avoid placing it next to radiators or vents. | Wood expands/contracts with moisture changes—this can warp keys, action parts, and affect tuning stability. | | **Tuning Frequency** | • Tune at least twice per year if used regularly; once yearly for occasional use.
• For professional players or concert instruments, consider monthly tunings. | Piano strings stretch over time; regular tuning keeps intonation accurate and prevents “dead” notes. | | **Cleaning Routine** | • Dust gently with a microfiber cloth after each play session.
• Wipe down the lid, pedals, and bench with a slightly dampened cloth only when necessary.
• Never spray water on the keyboard surface. | Prevents dust buildup which can interfere with key action and cause corrosion on metal components. | | **Key Action Care** | • Check for sticky or uneven keys during tuning sessions.
• If a key feels sluggish, have a technician inspect the hammers and escapement mechanism. | Smooth action ensures expressive playing and reduces wear on internal parts. | | **Pedal Inspection** | • Inspect pedal cables and connections for fraying or loose contacts.
• Ensure footrests remain level and stable. | Pedals influence sustain and expression; faulty pedaling can damage strings or reduce sound quality. | | **String Tension Checks** | • During tuning, listen for buzzing or rattling sounds indicating broken or misaligned strings.
• Have a pro replace any damaged strings immediately. | Broken strings can produce unpleasant tones and may harm other structural elements. | | **Professional Servicing** | • Schedule a full service (action reset, voicing, regulation) every 2–5 years depending on usage intensity.
• A qualified technician will also check the frame, bridge, and soundboard integrity. | Comprehensive servicing corrects long-term mechanical drift and preserves tonal richness. | | **Environmental Protection** | • Cover the piano with a breathable cover when not in use.
• Move the piano away from direct sunlight or heat sources. | Covers protect against dust while allowing airflow; extreme temperatures accelerate wood warping. | ### Quick Checklist for Homeowners: 1. **Check Humidity:** Aim for 50 %. 2. **Tune Regularly:** At least biannually. 3. **Dust After Play:** Light touch, never wet. 4. **Inspect Keys/Pedals Weekly:** Spot any sticking or wobbling. 5. **Schedule Professional Service Every 3 Years** (or sooner if heavily played). By following this routine, you'll help preserve both the mechanics and the beautiful tone of your piano for many decades!
message.reasoning:
The user asks "What are some tips to maintain a piano?" They want general maintenance advice. We can provide them with tips like humidity control, tuning frequency, cleaning, etc.

We don't need to call any tool because it's not about retrieving data from an external source; we just give general knowledge. So no function calls needed. We'll answer directly.
